Written comments may be submitted to the Zoning Board via regular mail addressed to: Zoning Board of Review, Bristol Town Hall, 10 Court Street, Bristol, RI 02809 or via email to etanner@bristolri.gov. Written comments should be received no later than 12:00 p.m. on October 1st, 2026. 1. Pledge of Allegiance 2. Approval of Minutes - September 14, 2026 3. Sitting as Board of Appeal - Continued Petitions 4. 3A. ZAPL-26-1, ZAPL-26-3, ZAPL-26-4 David Ramos / Ramos Landscaping, LLC – Appeal (continued from July 13th): of three Notices of Violation dated February 12th, February 25th, and March 11, 2026 issued by the Administrative Officer for conducting business operations on a Sunday and/or outside of the Planning Board’s approved special use permit hours of operation. Located at 668 and 670 Metacom Avenue; Assessor’s Plat 128, Lots 15 & 16; Zone: GB. Public Hearing is closed, vote on formal decision only. 3B. ZAPL-26-5 John J. The only way to guarantee complete access to the meeting is to attend physically, in person, at the physical location listed on the agenda. The public is welcome to participate in Town Council meetings in several ways: • Citizens are invited to speak on the topic of a Public Hearing, which will be listed on the agenda. • Citizens may speak during Open Forum to clarify or comment on an item on the agenda or address items not on the agenda. o A Citizen may schedule a Request to Address with the Town Council no less than seven days before the meeting in which they would like to appear. Their topic will be listed on the agenda, and Town Councilors may respond to their comments. o Citizens may also simply request to speak in Open Forum at a Council meeting by raising their hands and being recognized by the Town Council President. (See below) • At other times during a Town Council meeting, citizens may speak at the discretion of the Council President or of a majority of Councilors present. Anyone wishing to speak should use the microphone at the front of the room and state their name and address for the record. Comments must be addressed to the Council, not the audience. The Town Council hopes that citizens and Councilors alike will be respectful of each other and mindful of everyone’s time. For those speaking on an agenda item, please note that this is the time reserved for councilors to discuss the item, and your participation in the discussion is at the Council's discretion. Item # 9 ORDINANCE OF THE TOWN OF MIDDLETOWN, RHODE ISLAND AN ORDINANCE AMENDING THE TOWN CODE OF THE TOWN OF MIDDLETOWN TITLE XV LAND USAGE Chapter 152, Zoning Code NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED AS FOLLOWS: FIRST: That Town Code Title XV, Land Usage, is hereby amended by (1) amending Sections Section 152.01, Appendix A, Article 7, Section 728 entitled “Adaptive Reuse of Commercial Buildings”, as follows (language to be deleted is stricken out within brackets; language to be added is underlined and presented in red ink): CHAPTER 152: ZONING CODE, APPENDIX A, ARTICLE 7, SUPPLEMENTARY REGULATIONS § 728 Adaptive Reuse of Commercial Buildings. (A) Notwithstanding any other provisions of this chapter, adaptive reuse for the conversion of any commercial building, including offices, schools, religious facilities, medical buildings, and malls into residential units or mixed use developments which include the development of at least 50% of the existing gross floor area into residential units, shall be a permitted use in all districts and allowed subject to provisions of this section, except where such use is prohibited by environmental land use restrictions recorded on the property by the State of Rhode Island Department of Environmental Management or the United States Environmental Protection Agency preventing the conversion to residential use. (B) All adaptive reuse projects are subject to development plan review, and must comply with all other applicable requirements of this chapter except as indicated in this section. (C) Adaptive reuse developments shall be required to provide one off-street parking space per dwelling unit. (D) Density. (1) For projects that meet the following criteria, high density development is permitted up to 15 dwelling units per acre; (a) Where the project is limited to the existing building footprint, except that the footprint is allowed to be expanded to accommodate upgrades related to the building and fire codes and utilities; and (b) The development includes at least 20% low- and moderate-income housing; and (c) The development has access to public sewer and water service or has access to adequate private water, such as a well and/or wastewater treatment systems(s) approved by the relevant state agency for the entire development as applicable. (2) For all other adaptive reuse projects, the residential density permitted in the converted structure shall be the maximum allowed that otherwise meets all standards of minimum housing and has access to public sewer and water service or has access to adequate private water, such as a well, and wastewater treatment system(s) approved by the relevant state agency for the entire development, as applicable. The density proposed shall be determined to meet all public health and safety standards. (E) Notwithstanding any other provisions of this chapter, for adaptive reuse projects, existing building setbacks shall remain and shall be considered legal nonconforming, but no additional encroachments shall be permitted into any nonconforming setback, unless otherwise allowed by zoning ordinance or relief is granted by the applicable authority. (F) For adaptive reuse projects, notwithstanding any other provisions of this chapter, the height of the existing structure, if it exceeds the maximum height of the zoning district, may remain and shall be considered legal nonconforming, and any rooftop construction shall be included within the height exemption. (G) Residential units in adaptive reuse projects shall not be offered or rented for short-term rental, tourist or transient use or through a hosting platform, as such terms are defined in R.I. Gen. Laws § 42-63.1-2. SECOND: This ordinance shall take effect upon its adoption and all ordinances or parts of ordinances inconsistent herewith are hereby repealed. Item #15 ORDINACE OF THE TOWN OF MIDDLETOWN, RHODE ISLAND AN ORDINANCE AMENDING THE TOWN CODE OF THE TOWN OF MIDDLETOWN TITLE IV: GENERAL REGULATIONS NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED AS FOLLOWS: FIRST: The following new section is inserted into Title IV, Chapter 94: Streets Sidewalks and Public Places: Section 94.08: GREEN AND COMPLETE STREETS POLICY STATEMENT Section 94.08 (1) Legislative Findings and Intent 94.08 (2) Definitions 94.08 (3) Green and Complete Streets Requirements 94.08 (4) Exceptions 94.08 (5) Implementation 1. Legislative Findings and Intent. (a) The Town of Middletown is committed to increasing the safety and accessibility of its streets, roads and overall transportation systems for all users. (b) The benefits of adopting a Green and Complete Streets approach to transportation to guide investments and decision-making for the Town’s transportation system to include increased safety and accessibility to multimodal transportation and access to destinations such as job centers and health or educational facilities; increased opportunity for active living, exercise, and recreation through waking and bicycling; economic benefits from walkable commercial areas and neighborhoods, better access to recreational areas, parks and beaches; and environmental, climate change and quality of life benefits. (c) The Town Council intends, by the enactment of this ordinance and the adoption of a Green and Complete Streets approach to transportation, to protect the public health, safety, and welfare of all residents and visitors. 2. Definitions. – As used in this Ordinance. (a) “Green and Complete Streets” means an approach to transportation that calls for the planning, design, construction, maintenance and operation of streets, roads, highways, and other transportation facilities to serve multiple modes of transportation, to meet the needs of all users, including all ages and abilities, and to provide safe access and mobility while also incorporating green infrastructure elements. (b) “All Users” means all persons walking, rolling, bicycling, taking public transportation, driving or being transported by motorized vehicles or transportation freight or commercial vehicles, and includes persons of all ages and abilities. (c) “Accommodation” means an element or aspect of transportation design, management, maintenance, or operation that serves the needs of a user identified as a member of All Users. (d) “Transportation Facility” means any existing or new highway, road, trail, path, bridge, tunnel, overpass, ferry, mass transit facility, parking facility, rail facility, intermodal facility, or similar facility open to the public and used for the transportation of persons or goods, together with any buildings, structures, parking areas, appurtenances, or other property needed to operate such a facility. 3. Green and Complete Streets Principles. (a) Pedestrian, bicycle, and motorized vehicle modes, including those providing public transportation or carrying freight, are integral to the Town’s transportation system, and the transportation system serves All Users. Therefore, the Town shall work to create a safe, comprehensive, integrated, and connected network that accommodates the needs or all users. (b) The applicable Departments of the Town shall consider all transportation funding programs and transportation improvement projects undertaken within the Town and opportunities to improve the transportation system’s safety, accessibility, access to destinations, and mobility for all users. (c) The Green and Complete Streets approach shall be utilized in the planning, design, construction, reconstruction, rehabilitation, maintenance, and operation of any transportation facility under the jurisdiction of the Town. (d) Accommodations for all users should consider the Town’s current and expected future land uses and transportation needs and should provide access to destinations such as job centers, health facilities, educational institutions, retail centers, or civic and community facilities. (e) A Green and Complete Streets approach includes consideration of, but is not limited to, the following: 1. Allocation of space among transportation modes. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. 7. Pedestrian facilities and design elements. Bicycle facilities and design elements. Public transportation facilities and design elements. American with Disabilities Act accessibility elements. Motorized vehicle safety design elements for drivers of all ages. Traffic calming design elements, such as narrower lanes and tighter turning radii. 8. Speed limit and design speeds. 9. Traffic control devices. 10. Lighting. 11. Stormwater management. 12. Maintenance procedures and policies. 13. Operations procedures and policies. 14. Parking management. 15. Freight uses and goods delivery management. 16. Access management. When evaluating these considerations, the intent should be for improvements that are consistent with the following Green and Complete Streets principles. 1. Encourage active mobility by promoting alternative modes of transportation, such as walking and cycling. 2. Provide adequate, safe and comfortable access to all transportation modes for all users. (f) The Town shall develop, revise, or update related plans, policies, specifications, procedures, regulations and guidelines to ensure that the Town’s transportation system serves the needs of all users. (g) In implementing this ordinance, the Town shall use the latest and most applicable design standards for Green and Complete Streets including the most recent editions of the following: 1. Urban Street Design Guide (National Association of City Transportation Officials) 2. Transit Street Design Guide (National Association of City Transportation Officials) 3. Urban Bikeway Design Guide National Association of City Transportation Officials) 4. Urban Street Stormwater Design Guide (National Association of City Transportation Officials) 5. Guide for the Planning, Design, and Operation of Pedestrian Facilities (American Associations of State Highway and Transportation Officials) 6. “Public Rights-of-Way Accessibility Guidelines (PROWAG)” (United States Access Board) 7. Designing Walkable Urban Thoroughfares: A Context Sensitive Approach: An ITE Recommended Practice (Institute of Transportation Engineers) 8. Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities (American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials) 4. Exceptions. The principles set forth in Section 3 hereof should be relaxed in the following circumstances: (a) Travel on the transportation facility by a pedestrian, bicycle, or motorized vehicle mode is prohibited by law; (b) The cost of a new accommodation would be excessively disproportionate to the safety need or probable use. (c) There is a demonstrated absence of future needs as determined by factors including current and future land use, protected user volumes, population density, and crash data. (d) Short-term, emergency repairs are necessary and temporary accommodation are not feasible. 5. Implementation. The Town shall endeavor to incorporate the principles set forth in Section 3 herein, subject to the exceptions set forth in Section 4, as and when ordinances of the Town concerning transportation and land development are updated in the ordinary course as appropriate. SECOND: This ordinance shall take effect upon adoption and its provisions shall supersede any inconsistent or contrary provisions in any other ordinance. (B) All adaptive reuse projects are subject to development plan review, and must comply with all other applicable requirements of this chapter except as indicated in this section. (C) Adaptive reuse developments shall be required to provide one off-street parking space per dwelling unit. (D) Density. (1) For projects that meet the following criteria, high density development is permitted up to 15 dwelling units per acre; (a) Where the project is limited to the existing building footprint, except that the footprint is allowed to be expanded to accommodate upgrades related to the building and fire codes and utilities; and (b) The development includes at least 20% low- and moderate-income housing; and (c) The development has access to public sewer and water service or has access to adequate private water, such as a well and/or wastewater treatment systems(s) approved by the relevant state agency for the entire development as applicable. (2) For all other adaptive reuse projects, the residential density permitted in the converted structure shall be the maximum allowed that otherwise meets all standards of minimum housing and has access to public sewer and water service or has access to adequate private water, such as a well, and wastewater treatment system(s) approved by the relevant state agency for the entire development, as applicable. The density proposed shall be determined to meet all public health and safety standards. (E) Notwithstanding any other provisions of this chapter, for adaptive reuse projects, existing building setbacks shall remain and shall be considered legal nonconforming, but no additional encroachments shall be permitted into any nonconforming setback, unless otherwise allowed by zoning ordinance or relief is granted by the applicable authority. (F) For adaptive reuse projects, notwithstanding any other provisions of this chapter, the height of the existing structure, if it exceeds the maximum height of the zoning district, may remain and shall be considered legal nonconforming, and any rooftop construction shall be included within the height exemption. (G) Residential units in adaptive reuse projects shall not be offered or rented for short-term rental, tourist or transient use or through a hosting platform, as such terms are defined in R.I. Gen. Laws § 42-63.1-2. SECOND: This ordinance shall take effect upon its adoption and all ordinances or parts of ordinances inconsistent herewith are hereby repealed. Item #15 ORDINACE OF THE TOWN OF MIDDLETOWN, RHODE ISLAND AN ORDINANCE AMENDING THE TOWN CODE OF THE TOWN OF MIDDLETOWN TITLE IV: GENERAL REGULATIONS NOW THEREFORE, BE IT ORDAINED AS FOLLOWS: FIRST: The following new section is inserted into Title IV, Chapter 94: Streets Sidewalks and Public Places: Section 94.08: GREEN AND COMPLETE STREETS POLICY STATEMENT Section 94.08 (1) Legislative Findings and Intent 94.08 (2) Definitions 94.08 (3) Green and Complete Streets Requirements 94.08 (4) Exceptions 94.08 (5) Implementation 1. Legislative Findings and Intent. (a) The Town of Middletown is committed to increasing the safety and accessibility of its streets, roads and overall transportation systems for all users. (b) The benefits of adopting a Green and Complete Streets approach to transportation to guide investments and decision-making for the Town’s transportation system to include increased safety and accessibility to multimodal transportation and access to destinations such as job centers and health or educational facilities; increased opportunity for active living, exercise, and recreation through waking and bicycling; economic benefits from walkable commercial areas and neighborhoods, better access to recreational areas, parks and beaches; and environmental, climate change and quality of life benefits. (c) The Town Council intends, by the enactment of this ordinance and the adoption of a Green and Complete Streets approach to transportation, to protect the public health, safety, and welfare of all residents and visitors. 2. Definitions. – As used in this Ordinance. (a) “Green and Complete Streets” means an approach to transportation that calls for the planning, design, construction, maintenance and operation of streets, roads, highways, and other transportation facilities to serve multiple modes of transportation, to meet the needs of all users, including all ages and abilities, and to provide safe access and mobility while also incorporating green infrastructure elements. (b) “All Users” means all persons walking, rolling, bicycling, taking public transportation, driving or being transported by motorized vehicles or transportation freight or commercial vehicles, and includes persons of all ages and abilities. (c) “Accommodation” means an element or aspect of transportation design, management, maintenance, or operation that serves the needs of a user identified as a member of All Users. (d) “Transportation Facility” means any existing or new highway, road, trail, path, bridge, tunnel, overpass, ferry, mass transit facility, parking facility, rail facility, intermodal facility, or similar facility open to the public and used for the transportation of persons or goods, together with any buildings, structures, parking areas, appurtenances, or other property needed to operate such a facility. 3. Green and Complete Streets Principles. (a) Pedestrian, bicycle, and motorized vehicle modes, including those providing public transportation or carrying freight, are integral to the Town’s transportation system, and the transportation system serves All Users. Therefore, the Town shall work to create a safe, comprehensive, integrated, and connected network that accommodates the needs or all users. (b) The applicable Departments of the Town shall consider all transportation funding programs and transportation improvement projects undertaken within the Town and opportunities to improve the transportation system’s safety, accessibility, access to destinations, and mobility for all users. (c) The Green and Complete Streets approach shall be utilized in the planning, design, construction, reconstruction, rehabilitation, maintenance, and operation of any transportation facility under the jurisdiction of the Town. (d) Accommodations for all users should consider the Town’s current and expected future land uses and transportation needs and should provide access to destinations such as job centers, health facilities, educational institutions, retail centers, or civic and community facilities. (e) A Green and Complete Streets approach includes consideration of, but is not limited to, the following: 1. Allocation of space among transportation modes. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. 7. Pedestrian facilities and design elements. Bicycle facilities and design elements. Public transportation facilities and design elements. American with Disabilities Act accessibility elements. Motorized vehicle safety design elements for drivers of all ages. Traffic calming design elements, such as narrower lanes and tighter turning radii. 8. Speed limit and design speeds. 9. Traffic control devices. 10. Lighting. 11. Stormwater management. 12. Maintenance procedures and policies. 13. Operations procedures and policies. 14. Parking management. 15. Freight uses and goods delivery management. 16. Access management. When evaluating these considerations, the intent should be for improvements that are consistent with the following Green and Complete Streets principles. 1. Encourage active mobility by promoting alternative modes of transportation, such as walking and cycling. 2. Provide adequate, safe and comfortable access to all transportation modes for all users. (f) The Town shall develop, revise, or update related plans, policies, specifications, procedures, regulations and guidelines to ensure that the Town’s transportation system serves the needs of all users. (g) In implementing this ordinance, the Town shall use the latest and most applicable design standards for Green and Complete Streets including the most recent editions of the following: 1. Urban Street Design Guide (National Association of City Transportation Officials) 2. Transit Street Design Guide (National Association of City Transportation Officials) 3. Urban Bikeway Design Guide National Association of City Transportation Officials) 4. Urban Street Stormwater Design Guide (National Association of City Transportation Officials) 5. Guide for the Planning, Design, and Operation of Pedestrian Facilities (American Associations of State Highway and Transportation Officials) 6. “Public Rights-of-Way Accessibility Guidelines (PROWAG)” (United States Access Board) 7. Designing Walkable Urban Thoroughfares: A Context Sensitive Approach: An ITE Recommended Practice (Institute of Transportation Engineers) 8. Guide for the Development of Bicycle Facilities (American Association of State Highway and Transportation Officials) 4. Exceptions. The principles set forth in Section 3 hereof should be relaxed in the following circumstances: (a) Travel on the transportation facility by a pedestrian, bicycle, or motorized vehicle mode is prohibited by law; (b) The cost of a new accommodation would be excessively disproportionate to the safety need or probable use. (c) There is a demonstrated absence of future needs as determined by factors including current and future land use, protected user volumes, population density, and crash data. (d) Short-term, emergency repairs are necessary and temporary accommodation are not feasible. 5. Implementation. The Town shall endeavor to incorporate the principles set forth in Section 3 herein, subject to the exceptions set forth in Section 4, as and when ordinances of the Town concerning transportation and land development are updated in the ordinary course as appropriate. SECOND: This ordinance shall take effect upon adoption and its provisions shall supersede any inconsistent or contrary provisions in any other ordinance. Applicants and their representatives as well as members of the public may attend in person or can access the virtual meeting by using the Zoom Webinar Platform at: https://providenceri-gov.zoom.us/j/94889627470 The Webinar ID is: 9 4 8 8 962 7470 A computer with a microphone is required for participation OR those without computer access may participate by telephone. Dial the following number and use Webinar ID 9 4 8 8 9 6 2 7 4 7 0 # when prompted: +1 312 626 6799 These virtual access options are being provided only as a convenience and not as an official “location” where access to the meeting is guaranteed. Being physically present at the meeting is the only way to guarantee access to the meeting. All matters appearing on the Agenda are scheduled for discussion and possible vote or other action. All persons interested will be heard for or against the granting of the following applications pursuant to Section 1703 of the Zoning Ordinance: I. BUSINESS MATTER - Approval of the meeting minutes of the August 12, 2026 ZBR hearing. II. NEW MATTERS 1. The Narragansett Electric Company (Applicant/Owner): 640 Allens Ave, Plat 101, Lot 1, located in a W-3 Port/Maritime Industrial Waterfront District. Application for DIMENSIONAL VARIANCES seeking relief from Sections 1301.D.1. and 1302.I.3.a. of the City of Providence Zoning Ordinance. The applicant proposes updating the existing Utility site with a storage yard area utilizing new 35-foot-tall pole lighting, where 25 feet is the maximum permitted, and new fencing that is topped with 3 strands of barbed wire where zero are permitted. 2. Steven Freels (Applicant/Owner): 48 Covell St, Plat 63, Lot 155, located in an R-3 Residential District. Application for DIMENSIONAL VARIANCES from Table 4-1 as modified by Section 2003.B., and Sections 1202.L.1. and 1302.J.3. of the City of Providence Zoning Ordinance. The applicant proposes a new three-family dwelling with integral garage bays in the location of an existing 4 bay garage structure. The proposed interior side setback is .19 feet where 3 feet are the required minimum, the integral garage doors have a width of 33 feet where 22 feet is the maximum permitted, and the entry on the side of the dwelling is 23 feet from the front façade where 20 feet are the maximum permitted. 3. PVD, LLC (Applicant/Owner): 144 Benefit St, Plat 10, lot 81, located in an R-3 Residential and HD Historic Overlay District. Application for DIMENSIONAL VARIANCE seeking relief from Table 14-1 of the City of Providence Zoning Ordinance. The applicant proposes renovating the existing building for use as a multi-family dwelling with 13 units on a lot with 6 existing parking spaces. Thus, relief is requested to provide 6 parking spaces where 13 spaces are required. 4. Wisdom Properties, LLC (Applicant/Owner): 23 Alger Ave, Plat 88, lot 137, located in an R-3 Residential District. Application for DIMENSIONAL VARIANCES seeking relief from Table 14-1 of the City of Providence Zoning Ordinance. The applicant proposes to construct a new two-family dwelling on the lot which is land locked and is atypically oriented with its long dimension parallel to the front lot line. Thus, relief is requested to provide 3 feet of front yard setback where 13.25 feet is the minimum, and 6 feet of rear setback where 30 feet is the minimum. IMPORTANT INFORMATION: • Documents for new matters can be accessed at: http://www.providenceri.gov/inspection/boards-of-review/. If needed, contact Alexis Thompson at 401-680-5376 or at athompson@providenceri.gov to make other arrangements to view the documents. • The public will have the opportunity to comment during the meeting in person OR through the electronic platform by computer or by telephone. Public comment may also be submitted prior to the meeting via email to athompson@providenceri.gov. Submissions will be entered into the record and discussed at the meeting. • The Board encourages comments to be submitted at least 24 hours before the meeting. Page 1 of 4 Ryan J. Holt Chair • • Brett P. Smiley Mayor Contact Alexis Thompson, Secretary to the Zoning Board of Review, at 401-680-5376 or athompson@providenceri.gov, if you have any questions regarding this meeting, or submission of comment. This meeting may be continued from day to day and time to time at the discretion of the zoning board of review. This meeting is accessible to all persons. Individuals requesting interpreter services must notify the office of the boards of review at 401-6805375, at least 48 hours in advance of the hearing date. Page 2 of 4 Ryan J. Holt Chair Brett P. Smiley Mayor CIUDAD DE PROVIDENCE - JUNTA DE REVISIÓN DE ZONIFICACIÓN AVISO DE REUNIÓN Y AGENDA HÍBRIDA EN PERSONA / VIRTUAL Se da aviso de que la Junta de Revisión de Zonificación estará en sesión el MIÉRCOLES, 7 DE OCTUBRE DE 2026 a las 5:30 PM EN 444 WESTMINSTER STREET Los miembros de la junta deben asistir en persona. Los solicitantes y sus representantes, así como los miembros del público, pueden asistir en persona o pueden acceder a la reunión virtual utilizando la plataforma Zoom Webinar en: https://providenceri-gov.zoom.us/j/94889627470 La identificación del seminario web es: 9 4 8 8 9 6 2 7 4 7 0 Se requiere una computadora con un micrófono para participar O aquellos sin acceso a la computadora pueden participar por teléfono Marque los siguientes números y utilice el ID del seminario web 9 4 8 8 9 6 2 7 4 7 0 # cuando se le solicite: +1 312 626 6799 Estas opciones de acceso virtual se proporcionan únicamente por comodidad y no constituyen un "lugar" oficial donde se garantice el acceso a la reunión. La única forma de garantizar el acceso a la reunión es estar presente físicamente en la misma. Todas las personas interesadas serán escuchadas a favor o en contra de la concesión de las siguientes solicitudes de conformidad con la Sección 1703 de la Ordenanza de Zonificación: I. ASUNTO COMERCIAL - Aprobación del acta de la audiencia de la Junta de Revisión de Zonificación (ZBR) del 12 de agosto de 2026. II. NUEVOS ASUNTOS 1. The Narragansett Electric Company (Solicitante/Propietario): 640 Allens Ave, Plat 101, Lote 1, ubicado en un Distrito Industrial Portuario/Marítimo W-3. Solicitud de VARIACIONES DIMENSIONALES para obtener una exención de las Secciones 1301.D.1. y 1302.I.3.a. de la Ordenanza de Zonificación de la Ciudad de Providence. El solicitante propone actualizar el sitio de servicios públicos existente con un área de patio de almacenamiento que utiliza nueva iluminación de postes de 35 pies de altura, donde 25 pies es el máximo permitido, y una nueva cerca que está rematada con 3 hilos de alambre de púas donde no se permiten. 2. Steven Freels (Solicitante/Propietario): 48 Covell St, Plano 63, Lote 155, ubicado en un Distrito Residencial R-3. Solicitud de VARIACIONES DIMENSIONALES según la Tabla 4-1, modificada por la Sección 2003.B. y las Secciones 1202.L.1. y 1302.J.3. de la Ordenanza de Zonificación de la Ciudad de Providence. El solicitante propone una nueva vivienda de tres unidades con garaje integrado en el lugar donde actualmente existe un garaje de cuatro unidades. El retranqueo lateral interior propuesto es de 0.19 pies, cuando el mínimo requerido es de 3 pies; las puertas de garaje integradas tienen un ancho de 33 pies, cuando el máximo permitido es de 22 pies; y la entrada lateral de la vivienda se encuentra a 23 pies de la fachada principal, cuando el máximo permitido es de 20 pies. 3. PVD, LLC (Solicitante/Propietario): 144 Benefit St, Plat 10, lote 81, ubicado en un Distrito Residencial R-3 y Distrito Histórico HD. Solicitud de VARIACIÓN DIMENSIONAL para obtener una exención de la Tabla 14-1 de la Ordenanza de Zonificación de la Ciudad de Providence. El solicitante propone renovar el edificio existente para su uso como vivienda multifamiliar con 13 unidades en un lote con 6 plazas de estacionamiento existentes. Por lo tanto, se solicita una exención para proporcionar 6 plazas de estacionamiento donde se requieren 13. 4. Wisdom Properties, LLC (Solicitante/Propietario): 23 Alger Ave, Plat 88, lote 137, ubicado en un Distrito Residencial R-3. Solicitud de VARIACIONES DIMENSIONALES para obtener una exención de la Tabla 14-1 de la Ordenanza de Zonificación de la Ciudad de Providence. El solicitante propone construir una nueva vivienda bifamiliar en el lote, que no tiene acceso directo a la vía pública y está orientado de forma atípica con su dimensión más larga paralela a la línea frontal del lote. Por lo tanto, se solicita una exención para proporcionar un retranqueo frontal de 3 pies, donde el mínimo es de 13.25 pies, y un retranqueo trasero de 6 pies, donde el mínimo es de 30 pies. INFORMACIÓN IMPORTANTE: • Se puede acceder a los documentos para asuntos nuevos en: http://www.providenceri.gov/inspection/boards-of-review/. Si es necesario, comuníquese con Alexis Thompson al 401-680-5376 o a athompson@providenceri.gov para hacer otros arreglos para ver los documentos. • El público tendrá la oportunidad de comentar durante la reunión en persona O a través de la plataforma electrónica por computadora o por teléfono.. También se pueden enviar comentarios públicos antes de la reunión por correo electrónico a athompson@providenceri.gov. Las presentaciones se ingresarán en el registro y se discutirán en la reunión. • La Junta recomienda que los comentarios se envíen al menos 24 horas antes de la reunión. • Comuníquese con Alexis Thompson, Secretaria de la Junta de Revisión de Zonificación, al 401-680-5376 o Page 3 of 4 • Ryan J. Holt Chair Brett P. Smiley Mayor athompson@providenceri.gov, si tiene alguna pregunta sobre esta reunión o la presentación de comentarios Esta reunión puede continuar día a día y de vez en tiempo a discreción de la junta de revisión de zonificación. Esta reunión es accesible para todas las personas. Las personas que soliciten servicios de interprete deben notificar a la oficina de las juntas de revisión al 401-680-5375, al menos 48 horas antes de la fecha de la audiencia. Page 4 of 4

text: Town of Richmond, Rhode Island 5 Richmond Townhouse Road, Wyoming, RI 02898 www.richmondri.gov PLANNING BOARD AGENDA October 7, 2026 – 5:00 p.m. Site Walk Assessor’s Plat 10D, Lot 26 0 Shannock Village Road The Town of Richmond Planning Board will conduct a site walk at 5:00 p.m. on Wednesday, October 7, 2026 at 0 Shannock Village Road, Assessor’s Plat 10D, Lot 26, in relation to the following application: Major Land Development Project – Shannock Mill Redevelopment Project – Application of Shannock Mill Project, LLC (applicant/owner), 113 Memorial Boulevard West, Newport, RI 02840 for a proposed Major Land Development Project at Assessor’s Plat 10D, Lot 26. The proposed major land development project consists of the creation of a mixed-use development. Pursuant to Article 5, Section 5.7 of the Land Development and Subdivision Regulations, the “Planning Board shall visit the site of the proposed development to see the existing conditions and special features of the property, to identify potential site design issues, and to discuss site design concepts.” Pursuant to Article 5, Section 5.7, Subsection 5.7.3, “[c]omments made during the site walk by Planning Board members, staff, or consultants are not official statements. No formal recommendation or decision shall be made during a site walk.” The public is welcome to any open meeting of the Town Council or its committees. title: Smithfield Town Council 2026-10-06 agenda (filed 2026-09-30 11:04 ET)
text: SMITHFIELD TOWN COUNCIL MEETING SMITHFIELD TOWN HALL 64 FARNUM PIKE TUESDAY, OCTOBER 6, 2026 6:00 P.M. – EXECUTIVE SESSION 7:00 P.M. – OPEN SESSION 6:00 P.M. EXECUTIVE SESSION AGENDA Convene into executive session to consider, discuss, and act upon matters pursuant to Rhode Island General Laws Section 42-46-5(a)(1) Personnel; to interview Eric Sparfven for possible appointment to a Town board or commission and to conduct Town Clerk and Town Manager Performance Evaluations, and Section 42-46-5(a)(2); Potential Litigation. 7:00 P.M. I. OPEN SESSION AGENDA Regular meeting reconvened at 7:00 p.m. - Announce any executive session votes required to be disclosed pursuant to Rhode Island General Laws, Sec. 42-46-4. II. Prayer III. Salute to the Flag IV. Emergency Evacuation and Health Notification V. Presentations: A. Vin Zibelli, Senior Center/Human Services Director - Food Drive Update VI. Minutes: A. Move that the minutes of the September 1, 2026 open session meeting be approved as recorded. B. Move that the minutes of the September 15, 2026 Executive Session held pursuant to Rhode Island General Laws Section 42-46-5(a)(1) Personnel; to interview David Viera for possible appointment or reappointment to a Town board or commission be approved as recorded and sealed. C. Move that the minutes of the September 15, 2026 open session meeting be approved as recorded. VII. Consider, discuss and act upon the following possible appointments and reappointments: None VIII. Public Hearings: A. Conduct a public hearing to consider, discuss, and act upon an amendment to Chapters 45 and 46 of the Code of Ordinances entitled “Historic District Commission” and “Historic Preservation Commission,” respectively. B. Conduct a public hearing to consider, discuss, and act upon an amendment to the Code of Ordinances to add Chapter 351 entitled “Outdoor Clothes and Book Donation Bins” sponsored by Council President John J. Tassoni, Jr. C. Schedule a public hearing on October 20, 2026 to consider, discuss, and act upon an amendment to Chapter 60 of the Code of Ordinances entitled “Municipal Court”. IX. Licenses: A. Consider, discuss, and act upon approving two (2) One-Day Beer/Wine Licenses for the Smithfield Senior Center as follows:   “Halloween Party” to be held on Thursday, October 29, 2026 from 12:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. “Christmas Party” to be held on Thursday, December 10, 2026 from 12:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m. The parties will take place at the Smithfield Senior Center, 1 William J. Hawkins, Jr. Trail from 12:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m., as applied, subject to all State regulations and local ordinances. X. Old Business: A. Consider, discuss, and act upon adopting a resolution for the institution of a policy for the negotiation and ratification of Collective Bargaining Agreements. XI. New Business: A. Consider, discuss, and act upon adopting a resolution to establish quarterly joint meetings between the School Committee and Town Council. B. Consider, discuss, and act upon authorizing a sole source purchase of an Actiflo Ferric Metering Pump #3 from the Maher Corporation in the amount of eighteen thousand, three hundred fifty-two dollars and zero cents ($18,352.00) to be funded from the Sewer Authority’s Repair and Replacement budget. C. Sitting as the Smithfield Water Supply Board, consider, discuss, and act upon authorizing the Town Manager to enter into contract with Beta Group of Lincoln, RI in the amount of one hundred, forty-one thousand dollars and zero cents ($141,000.00) for the 2027 Water Supply Management Plan Five-Year Update to be paid for from the Water Supply Board’s Operating Budget. D. Sitting as the Smithfield Water Supply Board, consider, discuss, and act upon authorizing the Town Manager to enter into Contract, through the Interlocal Purchasing System Contract #230601, with Berry Dunn, McNeil & Parker, LLC of Portland, ME in the amount of seventeen thousand, four hundred dollars and zero cents ($17,400.00) to conduct a water rate study to be funded from the Water Supply Board’s Operating Budget. E. Consider, discuss, and act upon authorizing payment of Town Aided Funds in the amount of one thousand dollars and zero cents ($1,000.00) to the Meals on Wheels of Rhode Island. F. Consider, discuss, and act upon authorizing payment of Town Aided Funds in the amount of twenty thousand dollars and zero cents ($20,000.00) to the Woonasquatucket River Watershed Council. G. Consider, discuss, and act upon authorizing payment of Town Aided Funds in the amount of two thousand dollars and zero cents ($2,000.00) to the Wildlife Clinic of Rhode Island. H. Consider, discuss, and act upon authorizing payment of Town Aided Funds in the amount of twenty thousand dollars and zero cents ($20,000.00) to TriCounty Community Action Agency. I. Consider, discuss, and act upon authorizing the Conservation Commission to work with the Town Planner on the design of trails and tree planting projects at 60 Austin Avenue. J. Consider, discuss, and act upon adopting a resolution establishing a Technology, Innovation and Efficiency Commission sponsored by Council Vice President Angelica L. Bovis. XII. Public Comment. XIII. Adjournment. AGENDA POSTED: September 30, 2026 The public is welcome to any meeting of the Town Council or its sub-committees. text: TOWN OF COVENTRY Conservation Commission Meeting -Organizational MeetingWednesday, October 21, 2026 6:00 PM This meeting will be convened In-Person in the Coventry Town Hall Annex Planning Conference Room located at 1675 Flat River Road, Coventry, RI. 1. CALL TO ORDER 2. EMERGENCY EVACUATION INSTRUCTIONS 3. APPROVAL OF MINUTES 3.1. 4. 5. None OLD BUSINESS FOR DISCUSSION, VOTE, AND/OR ACTION 4.1. Lake Updates 4.2. Possible Grant Applications/Opportunities 4.3. Lake Recreational Activities 4.4. Sewer Development 4.5. Stormwater Management - Upper Dam Pond 4.6. Forest Management Plan - Fire Safety 4.7. Public Access and the Coventry PD 4.8. Discussion on Ideas for Increasing Members PROJECT REVIEW FOR DISCUSSION, VOTE, AND/OR ACTION 5.1. "Center Point Commons" For comments to the Planning Commission Preliminary Plan, Major Land Development Owner: Starr Capital LLC Applicant: Connolly & Partners LLC AP 7, Lot 24; Zone CCPD (Coventry Centre Planned District) 2271 New London Turnpike Applicant proposes to develop three (3) multi-family residential buildings with a total of 215 units, and associated parking, utilities, landscaping, and infrastructure. A significant percentage of the proposed units will be deed-restricted as affordable. This project is the residential portion of the mixed-use "Coventry Centre" development that previously received Master Plan and Zone Change approval in September 2025. The Page 1 of 3 commercial portion at 666 Arnold Road (AP 7, Lot 23) is separate from and not included in this Preliminary Plan application and review process. 5.2. "The Dunes" (fka "Centre of New England" Parcel 3) For comments to the Planning Commission Preliminary Plan, Major Land Development Owners: Matthew J. McGowan, in Receiver for Catapult Realty, LLC & Commerce Park Realty, LLC Applicant: EG Home, LLC AP 14, Lot 65 (Parcel 3); Portion of AP 13, Lot 14 (Parcel 2); Zone BP (Business Park) Centre of New England Boulevard & Angelina Drive Applicant proposes to develop 24 duplex buildings, 4 triplex buildings, 20 four-plex buildings, and 7 eight-plex buildings on the 30.5-acre subject parcel (Parcel 3), for a total of 196 residential dwelling units. 18% of the proposed units will be deed-restricted as affordable, per agreement. The proposed development will also include parking, stormwater management, landscaping, community open space, site lighting, and other amenities. Public water and sewer access are anticipated. This project is part of the larger "Centre of New England" development that previously received Master Plan approval for 712 units across three lots (Parcels 2, 3, and 4) in October 2024. Additional stormwater management improvements are proposed for Parcel 2, though the proposed residential development on that lot is separate from and not included in this Preliminary Plan application and review process. Parcel 4 is also not part of this phase. 5.3. "Picozzi Plat" For comments to the Planning Commission Preliminary Plan, Minor Subdivision with associated Dimensional Variance Owner/Applicant: Domenico Picozzi AP 89, Lot 9; Zone RR-2 (Rural Residential) Read Schoolhouse Road Applicant proposes to subdivide a landlocked 8.24-acre lot into four buildable lots, each of which would be roughly 2 acres in size and host a single-family dwelling. The new buildable lots would be accessed from a proposed private cul-de-sac extending from the paved driveway linking the Washington Oak Elementary School to Read School House Road, with legal access guaranteed via easement. The applicant is seeking a Dimensional Variance for zero frontage. Therefore, the project will be heard via Unified Development Review in which both the Minor Subdivision and the Dimensional Variance will be decided by the Planning Commission. Page 2 of 3 6. title: Jamestown Conservation Commission 2026-10-21 agenda (filed 2026-10-15 07:36 ET)
text: Jamestown Town Council Candidates Forum: Focus on Environment and Conservation Jamestown residents are invited to attend a Candidates Forum and Question & Answer session featuring candidates for the Jamestown Town Council on Wednesday, October 21, from 5:00 PM to 7:30 PM in the Meeting Hall at the Jamestown Philomenian Library. Co-hosted by the Jamestown Conservation Commission and the Audubon Society of Rhode Island, the nonpartisan forum aims to give local voters a direct opportunity to hear from council candidates and ask pressing questions regarding the island's environmental priorities and sustainable future. Key topics scheduled for discussion include: • • • • Water Conservation & Quality: Managing local groundwater resources, protecting watersheds, and ensuring long-term safe drinking water supplies for the island. Public Access to the Shore: Addressing rights-of-way, shoreline preservation, and coastal resilience in the face of rising sea levels and storm erosion. The Future of Gould Island: Balancing conservation interests, historic preservation, and wildlife protection for Gould Island. Environmental Stewardship: Policies concerning open space acquisition, habitat protection, and local climate action plans. "Local decisions made by the Town Council directly impact our natural resources, coastal access, and community resilience," event organizers noted. "This Q&A session offers residents a vital platform to understand where each candidate stands on preserving Jamestown's unique natural heritage." Event Details: • • • • • What: Jamestown Town Council Candidates Forum (Q&A Session) When: Wednesday, October 21, 2026 | 5:00 PM – 7:30 PM Where: Meeting Hall, Jamestown Philomenian Library (26 North Road, Jamestown, RI) Hosts: Jamestown Conservation Commission & Audubon Society of Rhode Island Admission: Free and open to the public. All residents are encouraged to attend. For more information, visit the Jamestown Philomenian Library event calendar, contact the Jamestown Conservation Commission or the Rhode Island Audubon Society.

To view the meeting with no interaction: YouTube Live Stream The above virtual access option is being provided only as a convenience and is not an official “location” where meeting access is guaranteed. The only way to guarantee complete access to the meeting is to attend physically, in person, at the physical location listed on the agenda. The public is welcome to participate in Town Council meetings in several ways: • Citizens are invited to speak on the topic of a Public Hearing, which will be listed on the agenda. • Citizens may speak during Open Forum to clarify or comment on an item on the agenda or address items not on the agenda. o A Citizen may schedule a Request to Address with the Town Council no less than seven days before the meeting in which they would like to appear. Their topic will be listed on the agenda, and Town Councilors may respond to their comments. o Citizens may also simply request to speak in Open Forum at a Council meeting by raising their hands and being recognized by the Town Council President. (See below) • At other times during a Town Council meeting, citizens may speak at the discretion of the Council President or of a majority of Councilors present. Anyone wishing to speak should use the microphone at the front of the room and state their name and address for the record. Comments must be addressed to the Council, not the audience. The Town Council hopes that citizens and Councilors alike will be respectful of each other and mindful of everyone’s time. text: POSTED – OCTOBER 14, 2026 REGULAR MEETING OCTOBER 19, 2026 TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MIDDLETOWN, RHODE ISLAND The following items of business, having been filed with the Town Clerk under the Rules of the Council, will come before the Council at a regular meeting to be held on Monday, October 19, 2026 at 5:00 P.M. Executive Session; Promotional Ceremony, Presentations and Town Updates Immediately Following Executive Session and 6:30 P.M. Regular Meeting at the Middletown Town Hall, 350 East Main Road, Middletown, Rhode Island. Said meeting will be conducted in person. Virtual access will also be provided by telephone conference call/ webinar and members of the public may access and listen to the meeting in real-time by calling 1-877-853-5257 (Toll Free) or 1-888-475-4499 (Toll Free) and entering Meeting ID: 891 8983 2942 or on the web at https://us02web.zoom.us/j/89189832942; however, virtual access is being provided only as a convenience and is not an official "location" where access to the meeting is guaranteed. Being physically present at the meeting is the only way to guarantee complete access to the meeting, as the meeting will not be paused or rescheduled if the virtual access fails. If you choose to join the meeting by zoom or telephone, Council Rules allow for the Public to speak only during the Public Forum and Public Hearings. If calling in by telephone, pressing *9 raises your hand and pressing *6 will unmute. The items listed on the Consent portion of the agenda are to be considered routine by the Town Council and will ordinarily be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a member of the Council, or a member of the public so requests and the Town Council President permits, in which event the item will be removed from Consent Agenda consideration and considered in its normal sequence on the agenda. All items on this agenda, with the exception of the Public Forum Session, may be considered, discussed, and voted upon in executive session and/or open session. Pursuant to RIGL §42-46-6(b). Notice – “Nothing contained herein shall prevent a public body, other than a school committee, from adding additional items to the agenda by majority vote of the members. Such additional items shall be for informational purposes only and may not be voted on except where necessary to address an unexpected occurrence that requires immediate action to protect the public or to refer the matter to an appropriate committee or to another body or official.” Any person not a member of the Council, desiring to address the Council concerning a matter on the docket of the Council, not the subject of a Public Hearing, shall submit a written request to the Town Clerk stating the matter upon which he desires to speak. Persons are permitted to address the Council for a period not to exceed five (5) minutes. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE TO THE FLAG RECONSIDERATION The Middletown Town Council follows the codification of present-day general parliamentary law as articulated in Robert’s Rules of Order Newly Revised 10th edition (2000), together with whatever rules of order the Council has adopted for its own governance. The motion to reconsider is one of the motions that can bring a question again before an assembly, and is designed to bring back for further consideration a motion which has already been voted on: If, in the same session that a motion has been voted on, but no later than the same day or the next day on which a business meeting is held, new information or a changed situation makes it appear that a different result might reflect the true will of the assembly, a member who voted with the prevailing side can, by moving to Reconsider [RONR (10th ed.), p. 304-321] the vote, propose that the question shall come before the assembly again as if it had not previously been considered. (From Robert’s Rules of Order Newly Revised In Brief, Robert, Evans et al., De Capo Press, 2004) EXECUTIVE SESSION – 5:00 P.M. 1. text: *POSTED AND AMENDED – OCTOBER 14, 2026 POSTED – OCTOBER 14, 2026 REGULAR MEETING OCTOBER 19, 2026 TOWN COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF MIDDLETOWN, RHODE ISLAND The following items of business, having been filed with the Town Clerk under the Rules of the Council, will come before the Council at a regular meeting to be held on Monday, October 19, 2026 at 5:00 P.M. Executive Session; Promotional Ceremony, Presentations and Town Updates Immediately Following Executive Session and 6:30 P.M. Regular Meeting at the Middletown Town Hall, 350 East Main Road, Middletown, Rhode Island. Said meeting will be conducted in person. Virtual access will also be provided by telephone conference call/ webinar and members of the public may access and listen to the meeting in real-time by calling 1-877-853-5257 (Toll Free) or 1-888-475-4499 (Toll Free) and entering Meeting ID: 891 8983 2942 or on the web at https://us02web.zoom.us/j/89189832942; however, virtual access is being provided only as a convenience and is not an official "location" where access to the meeting is guaranteed. Being physically present at the meeting is the only way to guarantee complete access to the meeting, as the meeting will not be paused or rescheduled if the virtual access fails. If you choose to join the meeting by zoom or telephone, Council Rules allow for the Public to speak only during the Public Forum and Public Hearings. If calling in by telephone, pressing *9 raises your hand and pressing *6 will unmute. The items listed on the Consent portion of the agenda are to be considered routine by the Town Council and will ordinarily be enacted by one motion. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless a member of the Council, or a member of the public so requests and the Town Council President permits, in which event the item will be removed from Consent Agenda consideration and considered in its normal sequence on the agenda. All items on this agenda, with the exception of the Public Forum Session, may be considered, discussed, and voted upon in executive session and/or open session. Pursuant to RIGL §42-46-6(b). Notice – “Nothing contained herein shall prevent a public body, other than a school committee, from adding additional items to the agenda by majority vote of the members. Such additional items shall be for informational purposes only and may not be voted on except where necessary to address an unexpected occurrence that requires immediate action to protect the public or to refer the matter to an appropriate committee or to another body or official.” Any person not a member of the Council, desiring to address the Council concerning a matter on the docket of the Council, not the subject of a Public Hearing, shall submit a written request to the Town Clerk stating the matter upon which he desires to speak. Persons are permitted to address the Council for a period not to exceed five (5) minutes. PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE TO THE FLAG RECONSIDERATION The Middletown Town Council follows the codification of present-day general parliamentary law as articulated in Robert’s Rules of Order Newly Revised 10th edition (2000), together with whatever rules of order the Council has adopted for its own governance. The motion to reconsider is one of the motions that can bring a question again before an assembly, and is designed to bring back for further consideration a motion which has already been voted on: If, in the same session that a motion has been voted on, but no later than the same day or the next day on which a business meeting is held, new information or a changed situation makes it appear that a different result might reflect the true will of the assembly, a member who voted with the prevailing side can, by moving to Reconsider [RONR (10th ed.), p. 304-321] the vote, propose that the question shall come before the assembly again as if it had not previously been considered. (From Robert’s Rules of Order Newly Revised In Brief, Robert, Evans et al., De Capo Press, 2004) EXECUTIVE SESSION – 5:00 P.M. 1.
